title: Machining TITAN-1M in Inconel 625 on Haas UMC-750 with Kennametal Tools

partInfo.program: BB Aero (Building Blocks Aero) — aerospace training components

stockDimensions.note: Larger than standard TITAN-1M (was 0.75 in original)

features: Chamfers on all edges and holes

material.name: Inconel 625
characteristics: Low thermal conductivity — coolant and lubricity are critical
Coolant can literally make or break the operation

comparedTo.titanium: Inconel is much harder than titanium; standard SFM for Ti is ~175, Inconel is 50-100 conventional
comparedTo.15-5_PH: Similar difficulty tier as 15-5 PH stainless

operations.name: Face Mill — Top Datum Surface

tool.insertGradeDescription: Special blend carbide for superalloys — newer generation, consistent machining in Inconel

wiperInsert.purpose: Replaces one standard insert; has flat bottom (not radius) to produce mirror-smooth surface finish. Sits lower than cutting inserts to clean up after them.

tool.system: Duo-Lock (modular — screw-in carbide tips to save cost)

speedsFeedsInconel.note: Running at low end of range for tutorial/safety. In production, SFM would be raised and chip load adjusted for perfect finish.

operations.strategy: Single pass face mill across top surface to establish first datum. 4 inserts cut, then wiper cleans the finish.
tips: Use wiper insert for mirror finish on Inconel face milling
Start at low SFM and raise on machine while adjusting chip load for finish
This datum surface is the reference for all subsequent pocket/hole dimensions

operations.name: Pre-Drill Pocket Entry Hole

tool.note: For production volumes, switch to KenTIP or KenTIP FS insert drill to reduce per-hole carbide cost.

speedsFeedsInconel.note: Running at low end of range — 84 SFM, 0.004 FPR for safe, perfect hole in Inconel.

operations.strategy: Drill straight down to full depth without pecking. Through-spindle coolant flushes chips — no peck cycle needed. Drill breaks chips internally.
operations.purpose: Pre-drill pocket entry point so end mill drops straight in instead of helical ramping into Inconel (saves tool wear and time).
tips: Sketch a point in CAM at the pocket entry location, then use that point for drill location
Drill diameter must be larger than roughing end mill (0.75 drill > 0.5 end mill = 0.125 clearance per side)
No peck needed with coolant-through drills in Inconel — continuous drill to depth
140-degree point leaves a tapered bottom; end mill must clear this taper (plan depth accordingly)
Tell CAM you have a pre-drilled hole so end mill drops straight in

operations.name: Rough Pocket and Outside Profile

tool.note: Nicknamed 'Zombie Cutter' because it keeps going even when dull. Extreme durability in Inconel.

speedsFeedsInconel.note: 210 SFM seems high vs. conventional 50-100 SFM for Inconel, but advanced peripheral milling with small radial engagement makes it possible and consistent. They routinely run 200-400 SFM in Inconel with this approach.

depthOfCut.axial: Full depth — approximately 2.5x diameter (1.2 in deep for 0.5 in tool)
depthOfCut.radial: 4% of diameter step-over (0.020 in for 0.5 in tool)

operations.strategy: Peripheral (high-speed adaptive) milling. Drop full depth, small radial step-over, utilize entire flute length for stability/rigidity. Ramp into material rather than plunge. End mill drops into pre-drilled hole, then peripheral mills outward.
tips: NEVER plunge straight down into Inconel with an end mill — pre-drill or ramp in
Peripheral milling (full depth, small radial) is far superior to conventional (shallow depth, large radial) for Inconel
Full flute engagement gives stability and rigidity — allows 2-4x higher SFM than traditional
Small radial + full depth = consistent chip load, better tool life, faster cycle time
40 IPM feed rate in Inconel is very fast — possible only with advanced toolpaths
HARVI 3 runs for hours in Inconel even as it dulls

operations.name: Finish Pocket Floor and Walls + Spring Pass

tool.note: Uses a different HARVI 3 than roughing — fresh tool for perfect finish. Roughing tool gets dull in Inconel.

speedsFeedsInconel.note: Same SFM as roughing (210), but chip load dropped in HALF for finishing (0.002 vs 0.004). Feed rate drops from 40 IPM to 19 IPM.

operations.strategy: Ramps into pocket bottom, finishes floor with wider step-over (since only 0.005 material to remove). Finishes inside walls full depth, then spring pass on walls to catch deflection. Then 2D contour full depth on outside profile + spring pass.
tips: Use separate fresh tool for finishing in Inconel — roughing tool will be dull
Drop feed per tooth in half for finishing (keep SFM same)
Wider step-over on floor finish is OK since minimal material
ALWAYS do spring pass on walls in Inconel — tool deflection leaves bottom of pocket undersized
Spring pass catches deflection without cutting extra material
2D contour for outside profile with 0.005 finish pass + spring pass
Walls must be perfect and perpendicular to top datum surface

operations.name: Pre-Drill Thread Holes (5/16-18 Minor Diameter)

tool.note: 0.257 in is the minor ID for 5/16-18 UNC thread

speedsFeedsInconel.note: Smaller drills get slightly less aggressive feeds — 0.002 to 0.003 FPR. Split the difference at 0.0025.

operations.strategy: Drill straight down without pecking (coolant-through). No spot drill or center drill needed — GO Drill is self-centering. Strategic decision: drill FIRST, then chamfer AFTER, because Inconel would rapidly wear a center drill/spot drill tip.
tips: GO Drill is self-centering — no spot drill needed in Inconel
In Inconel, drill first then chamfer (opposite of aluminum where you spot drill first)
Don't send a center drill or spot drill tip into Inconel — it will wear out fast
Smaller drills in Inconel: reduce feed per rev to 0.002-0.003 range
No peck cycle with through-coolant drills — blast chips out continuously

operations.name: Chamfer All Edges and Thread Holes

tool.system: Duo-Lock modular (screw-in tip, saves carbide cost)

speedsFeedsInconel.note: Lower SFM (60) when chamfering into holes — prevents chatter when tool hits full diameter engagement. Keep RPM low for pressure/engagement.

operations.strategy: Walk around all edges on part (outside contour, pocket edges) then chamfer the thread holes. For hole chamfering, use a programming trick: tell CAM the tool is larger diameter so it positions closer to wall, engaging flutes higher up for better cutting and bigger chamfer.
tips: Chamfer everything inside the machine in Inconel — no hand deburring
90-degree included angle: 45 per side, so chamfer depth = chamfer width (easy math)
In Inconel, use the flutes higher up on the chamfer mill body for holes — better rigidity
Programming trick: define a larger tool diameter in CAM to position tool closer to wall for deeper chamfer engagement
Back off RPM on hole chamfering to prevent chatter when full engagement hits
Keep RPM low to create cutting pressure — prevents tool bounce in Inconel
Duo-Lock system saves 50%+ on carbide cost in production

operations.name: Thread Mill 5/16-18 UNC Threads

tool.note: Full-form thread mill with many teeth, specifically designed for 5/16-18. Smaller than hole (0.242 vs 0.257) for safe entry/exit.

speedsFeedsInconel.note: 180 SFM is aggressive for a thread mill in Inconel but works with the proper technique.

operations.strategy: 3-pass thread milling strategy in Inconel: (1) Roughing pass leaving 0.005 stock, (2) Finish pass removing final 0.005, (3) Spring pass at same diameter to catch deflection. Each pass: drop to bottom, helical interpolate one revolution at 5/16 major diameter while Z rises 0.0556 per revolution. Through-coolant flushes chips from bottom up as tool lifts.
tips: Thread mill over tap in Inconel — adjustable, less catastrophic if it breaks
Thread mill breaks at neck (above threads) so part is salvageable; broken tap destroys the part
Thread mill allows compensation for plating/coating thickness
3-pass strategy: rough (leave 0.005) + finish + spring pass for perfect thread in Inconel
Spring pass catches any deflection from tool hanging out long in tough material
Through-coolant flushes chips from bottom of hole as tool helicals upward
Full-form thread mills cut all threads in one helical revolution — very fast
Thread gauge check (go/no-go) passed perfectly after thread milling
Helical Z rise = 1/TPI = 1/18 = 0.0556 per 360 degrees
Clearance between tool (0.242) and hole (0.257) is only 0.015 — plan chip evacuation

toolSystems.description: Modular end mill system — screw-in carbide tips on reusable body. Saves 50%+ on carbide in production. When tool wears, only replace the tip, not the entire tool.
Multi-purpose solid carbide coolant-through drill. Self-centering (no spot drill needed). Works in steels, stainless, titanium, Inconel, Monel.
Insert drill for high-volume production. Lower per-hole cost since only inserts are replaced. Recommended over GO Drill for thousands of parts.

insertGrades.application: Face milling Inconel 625 — new generation carbide blend for consistent aerospace superalloy machining

endMillLines.application: Roughing and finishing Inconel. Extreme durability — nicknamed 'Zombie Cutter' for relentless cutting even as it dulls.

notes: Coolant is the single most critical factor in Inconel machining — can make or break the operation
Through-tool coolant on ALL drills eliminates peck cycles entirely
Coolant flushes chips from bottom of holes during thread milling
Flood coolant supplementing TSC on all operations
High nickel content means heat stays in workpiece — coolant provides both cooling and lubricity

roughing.name: Peripheral / Adaptive Milling (High-Speed Machining style)
characteristics: Full axial depth of cut (2.5x diameter)
Small radial step-over (4% of diameter = 0.020 in on 0.5 in tool)
Utilize entire flute length for stability
Drop into pre-drilled hole to avoid helical entry in Inconel
advantages: Consistent chip load and tool engagement
Better tool life (cutter runs for hours)

finishing.name: 2D Contour + Floor Finish
characteristics: Half the chip load (0.002 vs 0.004 per tooth)
Spring pass on all walls to catch deflection

springPass.description: Final pass at same dimensions as finish pass. Cuts no programmed material — catches leftover stock from tool deflection. Essential in Inconel due to cutting forces causing deflection, especially at bottom of deep walls.

orderOfOperations: 2. Pre-drill pocket entry hole (3/4 GO Drill, larger than end mill)
3. Rough pocket and outside profile (HARVI 3, peripheral milling)
4. Finish pocket floor, walls, and outside profile + spring passes (fresh HARVI 3)
5. Pre-drill thread holes at minor diameter (0.257 GO Drill)
6. Chamfer all edges and thread holes (Duo-Lock 5/8 chamfer mill)
7. Thread mill 5/16-18 threads (3-pass: rough + finish + spring)

inconelVsAluminum: Aluminum: spot drill → drill → ream. Inconel: drill first → chamfer after (protects tool tips)
Aluminum: helical ramp into pockets. Inconel: pre-drill entry holes to avoid helical entry
Aluminum: fast peck drilling. Inconel: no peck with through-coolant drills
Aluminum: single finish pass. Inconel: finish + spring pass on every wall
Aluminum: one tool can rough and finish. Inconel: use separate fresh tool for finishing
toolDeflection: Deflection causes walls to be tapered — perfect at top, undersized at bottom
Spring pass compensates for deflection without removing programmed material
Long tools in deep pockets deflect more — always spring pass in Inconel
costSaving: Duo-Lock modular system reduces carbide cost 50%+ in production
KenTIP insert drills cheaper per hole than solid carbide in high volume
Thread milling saves parts if tool breaks (vs tap breaking = scrapped part)

speedsFeedsSummaryTable.note: Low end of range for tutorial
Full depth, 4% radial, advanced peripheral milling
Half chip load vs roughing, same SFM
Reduced SFM for hole entry — prevents chatter at full engagement

tribalKnowledge.tip: Pre-drill pocket entries in Inconel — helical ramping wears the bottom of end mills excessively and takes a long time
In Inconel, drill first then chamfer (reverse of aluminum order) — center drills and spot drills wear out fast on the tip in superalloys
Through-coolant drills eliminate peck cycles entirely in Inconel — the drill breaks chips internally and coolant flushes them out
Peripheral milling with 4% radial and full depth in Inconel enables 200-400 SFM vs conventional 50-100 SFM — the key is full flute engagement for rigidity
Always use a spring pass on finished walls in Inconel — tool deflection makes the bottom of pocket walls undersized, spring pass catches this without cutting extra material
Use a separate fresh end mill for finishing in Inconel — the roughing tool will be dull even if it's still cutting, and will leave poor surface finish
For finish facing with a shell mill, use a wiper insert set 0.0028 lower than cutting inserts — produces mirror finish on Inconel datum surfaces
tribalKnowledge.context: Face milling Inconel 625 with Dodeca Mini + wiper

tribalKnowledge.tip: Thread mill over tap in Inconel: thread mills break cleanly at the neck (part salvageable), taps break inside the hole (part scrapped). Thread mills also allow size compensation for plating.
On chamfer mills in Inconel holes, reduce RPM before full engagement to prevent chatter — keep RPM low to create cutting pressure so tool engages material without bouncing
For chamfer mill in deep holes: tell CAM the tool has a larger diameter than actual — this positions the tool closer to the wall, engaging flutes higher up for better cutting and bigger chamfer
Pre-drill diameter should be larger than roughing end mill (e.g., 0.75 drill for 0.5 end mill = 0.125 clearance per side) to allow straight plunge past the drill point taper
KCSM40 insert grade is the current generation Kennametal recommendation for Inconel face milling — replaces older grades for consistent superalloy cutting
